solver: physics_model/flood_swe.py ShallowWater (semi-implicit free surface, C grid, upwind advection, implicit Manning, CG tol 1e-7)
paper: Chen, Nadimy, Heaney, Sharifian, Via Estrem, Nicotina, Hilberts, Pain (2025) Solving the discretised shallow water equations using neural networks, Advances in Water Resources 2025 (PII S030917082500017X); code github.com/Amin-Nadimy/Shallow_Water_Equations_NN4PDEs

terrain.dtm_source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 2022, 1 m, tiles TQ27ne TQ27nw TQ28se TQ28sw (environment.data.gov.uk), vertical datum ODN (m AOD)
terrain.transform: Inverse of UTM zone 30N + Inverse of OSGB36 to WGS 84 (9) + British National Grid

grid_4m.aggregation: mean DTM / building fraction >= 0.5 / mean roof height of building cells

terrain.hole_rule: nodata or < -2.0 m AOD -> nearest valid cell

buildings.block_rule: bed = DTM + max(roof height, 3 m) on building cells (building-block method; roofs are not flow paths)

terrain.landcover: grass / vegetation from geometry_model/geometry/south_kensington_core008_landcover_4m (4 m, core008.glb materials), nearest-4m on the 1 m grid

grid.index_to_domain_m: x = 480 + 1 * ix, y = 640 + 1 * iy (cell lower corner)

scenario.reference_event: 12 July 2021 London / Kensington & Chelsea cloudburst (about 40-50 mm in 90 min)
scenario.roof_runoff: excess over sewer capacity routed to nearest ground cell
